chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily the one from among you who teaches knowledge shall receive a reward equal to the reward of the student, and he shall have merit over him. Therefore, learn knowledge from the bearers of knowledge, and teach it to your brothers just as the scholars have taught it to you.

key_terms.الْعُلَمَاءُ: Scholars — the qualified religious authorities from whom knowledge should be received
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: Merit, virtue, superiority — the additional rank the teacher holds over the student
key_terms.الْمُتَعَلِّمِ: The learner/student — one actively engaged in learning religious knowledge
key_terms.حَمَلَةِ الْعِلْمِ: Bearers of knowledge — those trusted to carry and transmit authentic religious knowledge

ai.seo_question: Does the teacher of Islamic knowledge receive the same reward as the student?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a profound principle of reciprocal spiritual reward in the transmission of knowledge: the teacher earns a reward equal to that of the student while retaining additional merit. This hadith was addressed to the community of believers in early Islamic Kufa, where the transmission of religious knowledge from the Imams' circle was the primary means of preserving Islamic doctrine. The Imam's audience would have understood 'bearers of knowledge' (hamalat al-'ilm) as specifically referring to trusted scholars from the Imams' circle, not merely anyone claiming scholarship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one from you who teaches the knowledge, for him would be a Recompense similar to the Recompense of the student, and for him would be the merit upon him (as being his teacher). Therefore learn the knowledge from the bearers of the knowledge, and teach it to your brethren just as the scholars<sup>asws</sup> have taught it to you all’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following. “

Those of you who teach will have the same reward as those who learn in addition to his higher position over the student. Learn knowledge from those possess knowledge and teach it to your brethren just as the scholars have taught you.”
